mainTopic: Why שילה and both Temples were destroyed, from the three cardinal sins to שנאת חנם, and the comparison between the First and Second Temple generations.
overview: This amud continues a ברייתא about the sins that destroyed the holy places. It finishes the two sins of בני עלי at שילה: delaying the women's offerings, which the פסוק counts as גילוי עריות, and בזיון קדשים. It then says the מקדש ראשון fell because of עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים, and proves each sin from a פסוק. The מקדש שני, whose people learned Torah and did kindness, fell because of שנאת חנם. This teaches that שנאת חנם is as severe as all three of those sins. The גמרא asks whether there was also hatred in the First Temple era and answers that it was found only among the leaders. רבי יוחנן, רבי אלעזר and ריש לקיש then debate which generation was greater, and the restored Temple is brought as proof that the earlier one was. Finally, ריש לקיש blames the Babylonian Jews for not all returning with עזרא, which left the Second Temple with only a בת קול. רבי יוחנן answers that the שכינה would not have rested there anyway, citing 'יַפְתְּ אֱלֹהִים לְיֶפֶת', and the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Delaying the offerings counts as if they sinned with the women
steps.stepSummary: Even according to the view that בני עלי only delayed the women's bird-offerings, the פסוק treats it as if they lay with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Even according to the one who says] that they delayed their bird-offerings, still the verse treats them as if they lay with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence that began on the previous amud. It explains how בני עלי were guilty of גילוי עריות, the first sin that destroyed שילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women after childbirth had to bring bird-offerings (קינין) before they could return to their husbands. בני עלי delayed these offerings, which kept the women away from their husbands. The פסוק describes this as if they had actually sinned with the women, showing how serious the delay was.

keyTerms.meaning: Pairs of bird-offerings, here brought by a woman after childbirth
The verse treats him as if

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying בני עלי actually committed adultery. According to this view they only delayed the offerings. The פסוק simply counts the delay as being as bad as the act.

phrases.english: that they delayed their bird-offerings,
phrases.notes: Finishes the opinion begun on the previous section: even according to the one who says this is all they did.

phrases.english: nevertheless, the verse ascribes to them
as if they lay with them.
phrases.notes: Refers to the פסוק in שמואל א ב:כב, 'אשר ישכבון את הנשים'.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיהָא מַעֲלֶה עֲלֵיהֶן הַכָּתוּב כְּאִילּוּ שְׁכָבוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof, begun on the previous amud, that שילה had גילוי עריות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Delaying the women's purification offerings is treated by the פסוק as equal to גילוי עריות.

steps.title: Proof that בני עלי disgraced the sacrifices
steps.stepSummary: The second sin of שילה, בזיון קדשים, is proven from שמואל א ב:טו-יז. בני עלי's servant demanded raw meat before the fat was burned on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Disgracing holy offerings, as it is written: 'Even before they burned the fat, the priest's servant came and said to the man sacrificing: Give meat to roast for the priest; he will not take cooked meat from you, only raw. And if the man said to him: Let them first burn the fat, then take as much as you want, he would say: No, give it now, and if not I will take it by force. And the sin of the young men was very great before ה׳, for the men disgraced ה׳'s offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second sin of שילה, disgracing the holy offerings, and brings a פסוק to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fat (חלב) had to be burned on the מזבח first, and only after that could the כהנים take their share. בני עלי's servant grabbed meat before the fat was burned, and threatened force. The פסוק itself calls this disgracing ה׳'s offering, which is exactly בזיון קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: The fats that must be burned on the altar

steps.whatToRemember: שילה was destroyed for two sins: גילוי עריות (the women's delayed offerings) and בזיון קדשים (taking meat before the fat was burned).

phrases.english: Degradation of consecrated items, as it is written:
"Also, before they burned the fat,
the priest's servant came
and said to the man who was sacrificing:
Give meat to roast for the priest,
for he will not take cooked meat from you,
only raw.
And the man said to him:
Let them first burn the fat right away,
and then take for yourself whatever you desire;
and he would say to him: No, you will give it now,
and if not, I will take it by force.
And the sin of the young men was very great
before the Lord,
for the men treated with contempt
the offering of the Lord."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first sin of שילה (גילוי עריות) to the second (בזיון קדשים).
steps.raayaObject: The claim that שילה was destroyed partly because of בזיון קדשים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א ב:טו-יז: taking meat before the fat was burned, and 'נאצו האנשים את מנחת ה׳'.

steps.title: The three sins that destroyed the First Temple
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that the מקדש ראשון was destroyed because of עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות, and שפיכות דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why was the First Temple destroyed? Because of three things that were in it: idol worship, forbidden relations, and bloodshed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves from שילה to the מקדש ראשון and lists the three sins that caused its destruction. This opens a new section, and the גמרא will now prove each sin from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'מפני מה' is not an attack. It is the ברייתא's own way of introducing its teaching. These three sins are the most severe in the Torah, so they explain why the Temple was destroyed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the famous contrast, coming later on this daf, with the מקדש שני, which was destroyed because of שנאת חנם.

phrases.english: The First Temple, why was it destroyed?
Because of three things that were in it:

phrases.aramaic: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וְגִלּוּי עֲרָיוֹת, וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים.
phrases.english: idol worship, forbidden relations, and bloodshed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing שילה, the ברייתא turns to the next destruction, the מקדש ראשון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מקדש ראשון was destroyed because of עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות, and שפיכות דמים.

steps.title: Verse proving idol worship in the First Temple
steps.stepSummary: עבודה זרה is proven from ישעיהו כח:כ, 'כי קצר המצע מהשתרע'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Idol worship, as it is written: 'For the bed is too short for stretching.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins proving the first of the three sins, עבודה זרה, by quoting a פסוק. The meaning of the פסוק is not clear yet, and the next step will ask about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance, a short bed has nothing to do with idols. The proof only works once the unusual word מהשתרע is explained, so this step depends on the explanation that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: For stretching out (to be explained by רבי יונתן)

phrases.english: Idol worship, as it is written:
"For the bed is too short for stretching."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins supplying the source for the first sin listed in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That there was עבודה זרה during the מקדש ראשון.

steps.title: What does 'the bed is too short' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the unclear phrase in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'the bed is too short for stretching'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the strange phrase in the פסוק means. This sets up רבי יונתן's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real request for information, not a challenge. Without an explanation, it is hard to see how a short bed proves עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "the bed is too short for stretching"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the פסוק just quoted as proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the phrase 'קצר המצע מהשתרע' refers to עבודה זרה.

steps.title: רבי יונתן: one bed cannot hold two rulers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן reads מהשתרע as מהשתרר + רעים: the bed is too short for two companions to rule over it together. ה׳ and an idol cannot share one מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rabbi Yonatan said: This bed is too short for two companions to rule over it together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן answers the question. He explains that the פסוק describes an idol placed in the מקדש next to ה׳'s service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He splits the word מהשתרע into two words: מהשתרר (to rule) and רעים (companions). The 'bed' is the מקדש, and the 'two companions' are הקב"ה and the idol that מנשה placed there. The מקדש cannot hold both, so this proves there was עבודה זרה in the מקדש ראשון.
steps.whatToRemember: The מקדש ראשון fell for עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות, and שפיכות דמים. עבודה זרה is proven from 'קצר המצע מהשתרע': one מקדש cannot have two 'rulers', ה׳ and an idol.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan said:
This bed is too short
for ruling over it
two companions together.
phrases.notes: מהשתרע = מהשתרר + רעים‎: ה׳ and the idol cannot share one Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן: קָצַר מַצָּע זֶה מֵהִשְׂתָּרֵר עָלָיו שְׁנֵי רֵעִים כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 and completes the proof of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מהשתרע means 'two companions ruling together': the מקדש cannot contain both the service of ה׳ and an idol, so the פסוק refers to עבודה זרה in the מקדש.

steps.title: רבי יונתן weeps over the second half of the verse
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the ישעיהו פסוק, 'והמסכה צרה כהתכנס', is read as: an idol became a rival wife to ה׳‎. רבי יונתן cried when he reached this פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the cover is too narrow for gathering.' רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: when רבי יונתן reached this verse, he cried and said: 'The One about Whom it is written, "He gathers the waters of the sea like a heap," now has an idol as a rival?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining the ישעיהו פסוק by reading its second half. רבי יונתן is so pained by the meaning that he cries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מסכה (cover) is read as 'מסכה' meaning a molten idol. צרה (narrow) is read as 'צרה', a rival wife, like two wives of one husband. כהתכנס is linked to 'כונס כנד מי הים', which describes ה׳. The idea is that the all-powerful ה׳ was made to share His house with an idol, like a husband with a rival wife.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'cover'; read here as a molten idol
Literally 'narrow'; read here as a rival wife
'He gathers the sea's waters like a heap' (תהלים לג:ז), a description of ה׳'s power

phrases.english: 'And the cover is too narrow for gathering'
phrases.notes: The second half of ישעיהו כח:כ. Sefaria adds 'What is the meaning of' for clarity.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מָטֵי רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן לְהַאי קְרָא
phrases.english: When Rabbi Yonatan reached this verse
he cried and said:
The One about Whom it is written
'He gathers the waters of the sea like a heap'
phrases.notes: תהלים לג:ז, a word-play on כהתכנס.

phrases.english: an idol became a rival to Him?!
phrases.notes: A cry of pain, not a real question.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַמַּסֵּכָה צָרָה כְּהִתְכַּנֵּס אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the עבודה זרה פסוק begun in step 6, now covering its second half.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Meaning of the unclear words in the פסוק (from step 5).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מסכה = idol, צרה = rival wife: an idol was set up as a rival to ה׳ in His own house.

steps.title: Proof for forbidden relations from the daughters of Zion
steps.stepSummary: The second sin of the מקדש ראשון, גילוי עריות, is shown from ישעיהו ג:טז, which describes the immodest behavior of the daughters of Zion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Forbidden relations, as it is written: 'ה׳ said: Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with stretched-out necks and flirting eyes, walking with tiny steps, and making a jingling with their feet.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second of the three sins and quotes a פסוק to prove it. The next steps will explain each phrase of this פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in step 3 listed three sins. Step 4 proved עבודה זרה. Now the גמרא proves גילוי עריות through a פסוק describing women who behaved immodestly to draw attention.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughters of Zion (the women of Jerusalem)
Making a jingling or stamping with their feet

phrases.english: Forbidden relations, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ יַעַן כִּי גָבְהוּ בְּנוֹת צִיּוֹן
phrases.english: 'ה׳ said: Because the daughters of Zion are haughty'
'and walk with stretched-out necks'
'and flirting eyes'
'walking with tiny steps as they go'
'and making a jingling with their feet.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first sin (עבודה זרה) to the second (גילוי עריות).
steps.raayaObject: That the מקדש ראשון generation was guilty of גילוי עריות.

steps.title: Explaining the immodest behavior phrase by phrase
steps.stepSummary: Each of the first four phrases of the פסוק is explained as a specific immodest behavior meant to attract men.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Because the daughters of Zion are haughty': a tall woman would walk next to a short one so she would stand out. 'And walk with stretched-out necks': they walked standing very upright. 'And flirting eyes': they filled their eyes with blue eye-paint. 'Walking with tiny steps': they walked heel next to toe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains, phrase by phrase, what the women did. This shows why the פסוק proves גילוי עריות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase is turned into a concrete action: standing out by height, proud posture, eye makeup, and small attention-drawing steps. Together they show a culture of deliberately drawing men's attention, which led toward forbidden relations.

keyTerms.meaning: A tall woman walking next to a short one

phrases.english: 'Because the daughters of Zion are haughty' —
they would walk a tall woman beside a short one.
phrases.notes: So the tall one would stand out.

phrases.english: 'And walk with stretched-out necks' —
they would walk with an upright posture.
'And flirting eyes' —
they would fill their eyes with eye-paint.
'Walking with tiny steps as they go' —
they would walk heel beside toe.

steps.triggerLanguage: יַעַן כִּי גָּבְהוּ בְּנוֹת צִיּוֹן שֶׁהָיוּ מְהַלְּכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק quoted in step 8 to show how it proves גילוי עריות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each phrase of the פסוק describes a specific immodest behavior of the women of Jerusalem.

steps.title: רבי יצחק on the perfume in their shoes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains the last phrase: the women put perfume in their shoes and sprayed it at young men, putting the יצר הרע into them like snake venom.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And making a jingling with their feet': רבי יצחק said: they would bring myrrh and balsam and put it in their shoes. When they came near the young men of Israel, they would stamp and spray it at them, and put the evil inclination into them like the venom of an angry snake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק explains the last phrase of the פסוק. It is the strongest example of the women deliberately trying to tempt men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier phrases describe attention-getting behavior. This one describes actively targeting young men. The comparison to snake venom shows how quickly and deeply the temptation spread, which completes the proof of גילוי עריות.

keyTerms.meaning: Like venom of an angry snake (a viper)

phrases.english: 'And making a jingling with their feet' —
Rabbi Yitzchak said:
they would bring myrrh and balsam
and place them in their shoes,
and when they came near the young men of Israel
they would stamp and spray it at them,
and put the evil inclination into them
like the venom of an angry snake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the last phrase of the פסוק, completing the phrase-by-phrase reading from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The women used perfume in their shoes to tempt young men, spreading the יצר הרע like venom.

steps.title: Proof for bloodshed from King מנשה
steps.stepSummary: The third sin, שפיכות דמים, is proven from מלכים ב כא:טז: מנשה spilled so much innocent blood that Jerusalem was full from end to end.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bloodshed, as it is written: 'And also מנשה spilled very much innocent blood, until he filled Jerusalem from one end to the other.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the third and last sin of the מקדש ראשון with a פסוק about King מנשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This completes the proofs for all three sins listed in the ברייתא of step 3. Here the פסוק is direct and needs no explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: מנשה, a wicked king of יהודה
From one end to the other (literally 'mouth to mouth')

phrases.english: Bloodshed, as it is written:
'And also מנשה spilled very much innocent blood'

phrases.aramaic: עַד אֲשֶׁר מִלֵּא אֶת יְרוּשָׁלִַם פֶּה לָפֶה״.
phrases.english: 'until he filled Jerusalem from end to end.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the second sin (גילוי עריות) to the third (שפיכות דמים), finishing the list.
steps.raayaObject: That the מקדש ראשון generation was guilty of שפיכות דמים.
steps.whatToRemember: The מקדש ראשון was destroyed for the three cardinal sins: עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות, and שפיכות דמים. Each one is proven from a פסוק.

steps.title: Why was the Second Temple destroyed?
steps.stepSummary: The people of the מקדש שני era learned Torah, kept מצוות and did acts of kindness. So why was it destroyed?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the Second Temple, when people were busy with Torah, מצוות and acts of kindness, why was it destroyed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the מקדש שני and asks a question. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three sins explained the first destruction. But the second generation seemed righteous and did not commit those sins. So the reason for its destruction needs to be found.

phrases.english: But the Second Temple,
when they were busy with Torah
and מצוות and acts of kindness,
why was it destroyed?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל מִקְדָּשׁ שֵׁנִי שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹסְקִין בְּתוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with the מקדש ראשון: the three sins are not found in the second generation, so a new cause is needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The cause of the destruction of the מקדש שני, given that its generation was righteous.

steps.title: Because of baseless hatred
steps.stepSummary: The מקדש שני was destroyed because of שנאת חנם, baseless hatred between people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because there was baseless hatred in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the sin of the מקדש שני was שנאת חנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a generation full of Torah, מצוות and kindness can be destroyed because of hatred between people. Its religious behavior did not protect it from this one sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Baseless hatred, hating someone without a real reason

phrases.english: Because there was baseless hatred in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מקדש שני was destroyed because of שנאת חנם.

steps.title: Baseless hatred equals the three cardinal sins
steps.stepSummary: From this we learn that שנאת חנם is as severe as all three sins together: עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות, and שפיכות דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches you that baseless hatred is equal to the three sins: idol worship, forbidden relations, and bloodshed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson: since both Temples were destroyed, שנאת חנם must weigh as much as the three sins that destroyed the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first Temple needed all three cardinal sins to be destroyed. The second was destroyed by שנאת חנם alone. So שנאת חנם is equal in weight to all three combined.

phrases.english: To teach you that baseless hatred is equal
to the three sins:

phrases.aramaic: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, גִּלּוּי עֲרָיוֹת, וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים.
phrases.english: idol worship, forbidden relations, and bloodshed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson by comparing the answer of step 13 with the three sins of step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שנאת חנם weighs as much as עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות, and שפיכות דמים combined.
steps.whatToRemember: מקדש ראשון was destroyed for the three cardinal sins. מקדש שני was destroyed for שנאת חנם alone, even though people learned Torah and did kindness. So שנאת חנם is equal to all three.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the most famous lessons in Shas. It teaches that how we treat one another can be as serious as the gravest sins between man and ה׳.

steps.title: They were wicked but still trusted in ה׳
steps.stepSummary: A statement describes a generation that was wicked but still placed its trust in הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were wicked, but they placed their trust in the Holy One, Blessed be He.
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching continues with a short description of a generation: they did evil, yet they still trusted in ה׳. The very next line will tell us which generation this means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new detail to the picture. Wickedness and trust in ה׳ existed side by side in the same people. The statement does not name the era, so the גמרא will clarify it next.
steps.confusionAlert: The word 'they' does NOT refer to the מקדש שני people who were just discussed. The next line shows that it refers back to the מקדש ראשון generation.

phrases.english: They were wicked,
but they placed their trust
in the Holy One, Blessed be He.

steps.triggerLanguage: רְשָׁעִים הָיוּ, אֶלָּא שֶׁתָּלוּ בִּטְחוֹנָם בְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After concluding the topic of the מקדש שני, the teaching gives a new description that will turn out to refer back to the First Temple generation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A generation can be wicked in deeds and still rely on ה׳.

steps.title: This refers to the First Temple, as the verse in Micah shows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the previous statement as describing the מקדש ראשון era and proves it from מיכה ג:יא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now we have come back to the First Temple, as it is written: 'Her leaders judge for bribes, her priests teach for a price, and her prophets tell fortunes for money. Yet they lean on ה׳ and say: Is ה׳ not among us? No evil will come upon us.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that 'they were wicked but trusted in ה׳' is about the מקדש ראשון people. It brings a פסוק that describes exactly this mix.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק shows the wickedness: judges, כהנים and נביאים all took money. The second half shows the trust: they still said that ה׳ is among them. So the פסוק matches both parts of the statement.

keyTerms.meaning: They lean on or rely on

phrases.english: We have come back to the First Temple,
as it is written: 'Her leaders judge for bribes,
and her priests teach for a price,
and her prophets tell fortunes for money,
yet they lean on ה׳, saying:
Is ה׳ not among us?
No evil will come upon us.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies which generation step 15 describes and supports it with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That the 'wicked but trusting' description fits the מקדש ראשון generation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מיכה ג:יא: corrupt leaders, כהנים and נביאים, who still say 'ה׳ is among us'.

steps.title: Three decrees to match the three sins
steps.stepSummary: As a result, ה׳ brought three decrees on the First Temple people, one for each of their three sins, as מיכה ג:יב describes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the Holy One, Blessed be He, brought three decrees upon them, matching the three sins they had committed, as it says: 'Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become heaps of ruins, and the Temple Mount will be like forest high places.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the result: the punishment came in three parts, matching the three sins mentioned earlier. The proof is the very next פסוק in מיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three sins are the ones listed earlier: עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים. The פסוק lists three destructions: ציון plowed, ירושלים in ruins, and הר הבית overgrown. The punishment was measured exactly against the sins.
steps.whatToRemember: The מקדש ראשון fell because of three open sins, and ה׳ answered with three matching decrees.

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ הֵבִיא עֲלֵיהֶן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: Therefore the Holy One, Blessed be He, brought upon them
three decrees
matching the three sins they had committed,
as it says: 'Therefore, because of you,
Zion will be plowed like a field,
and Jerusalem will become heaps of ruins,
and the Temple Mount like forest high places.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִיכָךְ הֵבִיא עֲלֵיהֶן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שָׁלֹשׁ גְּזֵרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the outcome of the First Temple generation's behavior described in step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Three sins led to three matching decrees of destruction.

steps.title: Was there really no baseless hatred in the First Temple era?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that שנאת חנם was only a Second Temple sin, using a פסוק in יחזקאל and רבי אליעזר's explanation of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the First Temple era, was there no baseless hatred? But it is written: 'They are cast before the sword together with My people, therefore strike your thigh.' And רבי אליעזר said: These are people who eat and drink with each other, and stab each other with the swords of their tongues.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the clean split between the two Temples. It shows a פסוק suggesting that people in the First Temple era also hated each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that the מקדש שני fell because of שנאת חנם, implying this sin was not found in the First Temple era. רבי אליעזר reads the פסוק as describing friends who eat together but hurt each other with words. That sounds exactly like baseless hatred in the First Temple era.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it not written? (opens a challenge)
With the swords of their tongues (hurtful words)

phrases.aramaic: וּבְמִקְדָּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן לָא הֲוָה בֵּיהּ שִׂנְאַת חִנָּם?
phrases.english: And in the First Temple era, was there no baseless hatred?
But it is written: 'They are cast before the sword
together with My people,
therefore strike your thigh,'
and Rabbi Eliezer said:
These are people
who eat and drink with each other
and stab each other
with the swords of their tongues.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְמִקְדָּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן לָא הֲוָה בֵּיהּ שִׂנְאַת חִנָּם? וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the implied contrast between the Temples: if שנאת חנם existed in the First Temple era too, the distinction seems to fall apart.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that שנאת חנם was a uniquely Second Temple sin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק about the First Temple era, as explained by רבי אליעזר, describes people hurting each other with words, which is baseless hatred.

steps.title: That hatred was only among the leaders
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the hatred described in the פסוק existed only among the נשיאי ישראל, not the whole nation.
steps.simpleTranslation: That was among the leaders of Israel, as it is written: 'Cry out and wail, son of man, for it is among My people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting it. Yes, there was hatred, but only among the leaders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse quoted here is the beginning of the same פסוק from the challenge. Reading the whole פסוק in context shows that it is talking about the princes. So the nation as a whole did not suffer from שנאת חנם in the First Temple era.

keyTerms.meaning: The leaders or princes of Israel

phrases.english: That was among the leaders of Israel,
as it is written: 'Cry out and wail, son of man,
phrases.notes: Same פסוק as the challenge, יחזקאל כא:יז

phrases.english: for it is among My people,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 by narrowing who was involved.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope: the פסוק refers to a specific group, not the whole nation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק shows that the whole First Temple generation had baseless hatred.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the leaders had it, so the nation as a whole was not guilty of שנאת חנם.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms it was only the leaders
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the same פסוק and concludes that it refers only to the נשיאי ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: 'Cry out and wail, son of man.' You might think this applies to everyone. Therefore the verse says: 'It is upon all the leaders of Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support its answer. The ברייתא says directly that the פסוק is about the leaders, not about everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the classic pattern 'You might think... therefore the verse says.' It considers the possibility that everyone was included, then rejects it from the end of the פסוק. This backs up the answer in step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: In the First Temple era, baseless hatred existed only among the leaders. In the Second Temple era, it spread through the people.

phrases.english: And it was taught: 'Cry out and wail, son of man,'
might it apply to everyone?
Therefore the verse says:
'It is upon all the leaders of Israel.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: ״זְעַק וְהֵילֵל בֶּן אָדָם״, יָכוֹל לַכֹּל? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 19 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That the hatred in the פסוק was limited to the leaders.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that reads the end of יחזקאל כא:יז as 'upon all the leaders of Israel.'

steps.title: Open sin gave a known end; hidden sin left the end unknown
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר teach that the First Temple people sinned openly, so the end of their exile was revealed. The Second Temple people sinned in hiding, so the end of their exile was not revealed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר both said: The earlier ones, whose sin was revealed, had their end revealed. The later ones, whose sin was not revealed, did not have their end revealed.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give a new comparison between the two Temples. How openly each generation sinned affected whether the end of its exile was told to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The First Temple people did not hide their sins, and the נביא told them that their exile would end after seventy years. The Second Temple people hid their sin, such as hatred disguised behind friendly faces. So no end date was revealed for their exile, which we are still in.

keyTerms.meaning: Their end (the end of their exile)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the first exile had a known end of seventy years, while the current exile has no revealed end date.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַויְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar both said:
The earlier ones, whose sin was revealed,
had their end revealed.
The later ones, whose sin was not revealed,
did not have their end revealed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַויְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After separating the sins of the two Temples, the גמרא adds a new teaching about how those sins affected the length of each exile.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sin done openly led to an exile with a revealed end. Sin done in hiding led to an exile whose end is not revealed.

steps.title: The earlier generations were far greater
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that even the smallest part of the earlier generations is better than the biggest part of the later ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The fingernail of the earlier ones is better than the belly of the later ones.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after comparing the sins of the two Temple periods, רבי יוחנן makes a general statement about which generation was greater.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fingernail is the smallest, least important part of the body. A belly is large. רבי יוחנן means that the least of the ראשונים is better than the greatest of the אחרונים.

keyTerms.meaning: Fingernail. Here it stands for the smallest part.
Belly. Here it stands for the biggest part.
The earlier generation (the First Temple period)
The later generation (the Second Temple period)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The fingernail of the earlier ones is better
than the belly of the later ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the comparison between the First and Second Temple generations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ראשונים were vastly greater than the אחרונים.

steps.title: ריש לקיש says the later generations were better
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש argues the opposite: the later ones are greater, because they learn Torah even under foreign rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: On the contrary, the later ones are better. Even though foreign kingdoms rule over them, they are busy learning Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש pushes back against רבי יוחנן and says the later generation is actually greater.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning is that serving ה׳ in hard times is a bigger achievement. The אחרונים kept learning Torah even under שעבוד מלכיות, while the ראשונים had freedom.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to him:
On the contrary, the later ones are better,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיכָּא שִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכִיּוֹת —
phrases.english: even though there is subjugation by the kingdoms,
they are busy learning Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly disputes רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the ראשונים were greater
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Learning Torah while under oppression is a greater accomplishment, so the אחרונים should be considered greater.

steps.title: The Temple proves the earlier ones were greater
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן proves his view from history: the Temple was rebuilt for the earlier generation, but not for the later one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The Temple will prove it. It came back to the earlier ones, but it did not come back to the later ones.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש with a proof from what actually happened to the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the First Temple was destroyed, the people merited a second one. After the Second Temple was destroyed, it was not rebuilt. This shows that ה׳ considered the ראשונים more worthy.

keyTerms.meaning: The fortress/palace. Here it means the בית המקדש.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's proof is that the בית המקדש was restored after the first destruction but not after the second. So the earlier generations were greater.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The Temple will prove it,
for it was restored to the earlier ones
and it was not restored to the later ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוחנן defends his statement against ריש לקיש.
steps.raayaObject: That the ראשונים were greater than the אחרונים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The historical restoration of the בית המקדש after the first destruction only

steps.title: רבי אלעזר is asked the same question
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רבי אלעזר which generation was greater.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רבי אלעזר: Are the earlier ones greater, or are the later ones greater?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source on the same question. This line sets up רבי אלעזר's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same argument that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש just had. Now it is asked directly to another אמורא.

phrases.english: They asked Rabbi Elazar:
Are the earlier ones greater, or are the later ones greater?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel discussion of the same question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which generation was greater, the ראשונים or the אחרונים?

steps.title: Look at the Temple
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers with the same proof as רבי יוחנן, the Temple. The answer is recorded in two versions.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Put your eyes on the Temple. Some say he told them: The Temple is your witness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר points to the בית המקדש as the answer. The גמרא records two versions of his exact words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both versions, the point is the same as רבי יוחנן's. The Temple was rebuilt for the ראשונים and not for the אחרונים. The second version (איכא דאמרי) only changes the wording to 'your witness.'

keyTerms.meaning: Put your eyes on / look at

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר use the בית המקדש to prove that the earlier generations were greater.

phrases.english: He said to them: Put your eyes on the Temple.
Some say,
he said to them: The Temple is your witness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The restored Temple shows that the ראשונים were greater.

steps.title: ריש לקיש tells רבה בר בר חנה: I hate you Babylonians
steps.stepSummary: While ריש לקיש is swimming in the Jordan, רבה בר בר חנה offers him a hand, and ריש לקיש tells him he hates the Babylonian Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש was swimming in the Jordan. רבה בר בר חנה came and gave him a hand. ריש לקיש said to him: By God! I hate you (Babylonians).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about ריש לקיש in the Jordan River. He makes a strong statement against the Babylonian Jews, and the next step explains his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר בר חנה came from בבל. ריש לקיש's words are aimed at the Babylonian community as a whole. This sets up the פסוק he will bring to explain why.
steps.confusionAlert: 'לכו' is plural. ריש לקיש is not talking about a personal grudge against רבה בר בר חנה. He means the Babylonian Jews as a group, who did not come up with עזרא.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish was swimming in the Jordan.
Rabba bar bar Chana came
and gave him a hand.
He said to him: By God! I hate you all,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story about the weakness of the Second Temple generation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש resents the Babylonian Jews.

steps.title: A wall would have been silver, but doors are cedar
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains a פסוק in שיר השירים. If everyone had come up with עזרא together like a wall, they would have been like silver that never rots. Since only some came, like doors, they are like cedar, which rot can attack.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'If she is a wall, we will build on her a silver turret; if she is a door, we will cover her with a cedar board.' If you had made yourselves like a wall and all came up in the days of עזרא, you would have been compared to silver, which rot cannot attack. Now that you came up like doors, you are compared to cedar, which rot can attack.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש backs up his complaint with a פסוק, and explains what the פסוק means for the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wall is solid, while doors are only partial openings. Because the Jews of בבל did not all return together, the Second Temple received only a partial השראת השכינה. That partial presence is the 'cedar that can rot.'

keyTerms.meaning: Door (here, only part of the nation)
עזרא, who led the return to build the Second Temple

steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why the Second Temple lacked the full שכינה: the people did not return as one united nation.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'If she is a wall,
we will build on her a silver turret;
and if she is a door,
we will cover her with a cedar board.'
If you had made yourselves like a wall
and all of you had come up in the days of Ezra,
you would have been compared to silver,
which rot cannot attack.
Now that you came up like doors,
you are compared to cedar,
which rot can attack.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind ריש לקיש's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That the Babylonian Jews are to blame for the Second Temple's weakness

steps.title: What rot attacks cedar?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what rot it is that attacks cedar.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the rot of cedar?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a clarification of the cedar image. This sets up עולא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cedar is a strong wood, so the גמרא wants to know what kind of rot can attack it.

phrases.english: What is (the rot of) cedar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies a term from ריש לקיש's דרשה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the rot that attacks cedar?

steps.title: עולא: it is the ססמגור worm
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that the rot is the ססמגור, a worm that eats cedar.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: It is the ססמגור worm.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא names the worm that eats away at cedar wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ססמגור eats the cedar from inside until little is left. This image will be applied to the שכינה in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of worm that eats cedar

phrases.english: Ulla said: The sasmagor worm.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rot is the ססמגור worm.

steps.title: What does the ססמגור stand for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the worm represents in the Second Temple period.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the ססמגור (in this comparison)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the worm image applies to the Jewish people. This sets up רבי אבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the name of the worm is not enough. The גמרא wants to know what spiritual reality it describes.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the worm stand for?

phrases.english: What is the sasmagor (in this comparison)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a further clarification of עולא's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the worm-eaten cedar represent?

steps.title: רבי אבא: only a בת קול remained
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא explains that just as little is left of a worm-eaten cedar, only a בת קול was left of the שכינה in the Second Temple period.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: A בת קול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא explains that the worm image means only a small remnant of Divine revelation remained, a בת קול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Full נבואה was 'eaten away,' and only a weak echo of it was left. That is the partial השראת השכינה of the 'doors' generation.

keyTerms.meaning: A Divine voice/echo, a lower level than prophecy

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said: A Divine Voice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The remnant left in the Second Temple period was only a בת קול.

steps.title: After the last prophets, only a Divine Voice was left
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא confirms that after חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי died, רוח הקודש left Israel, and only a בת קול remained.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: After the last prophets, חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי, died, רוח הקודש left Israel. But they still used a בת קול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבי אבא's claim that only a בת קול remained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last prophets lived early in the Second Temple period. After them, true prophecy ended, and only the lower level of בת קול continued. This matches the image of the worm-eaten cedar.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: Because not everyone came up with עזרא, the Second Temple had only a partial שכינה. After the last prophets, only a בת קול remained.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Once the last prophets died,
Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi,
the Divine Spirit departed from Israel,
and they were still using a Divine Voice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אבא's answer with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That only a בת קול remained in the Second Temple period
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the end of prophecy after חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי

steps.title: Would ריש לקיש really talk with רבה בר בר חנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the story. ריש לקיש did not speak in public even with the great רבי אלעזר, so how could he have spoken with רבה בר בר חנה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And would ריש לקיש really talk with רבה בר בר חנה? Think about רבי אלעזר, who was the master of ארץ ישראל, and still ריש לקיש would not talk with him in public. ריש לקיש was so careful about this that if he was seen talking with someone in the marketplace, people would lend that person money without witnesses. And yet he would talk with רבה בר בר חנה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the river story and questions whether it could really have happened as told. It argues that ריש לקיש would never have held a conversation with רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a קל וחומר-style argument. ריש לקיש did not even speak publicly with רבי אלעזר, the leading sage of ארץ ישראל, so he certainly would not speak with רבה בר בר חנה. ריש לקיש's public conversation was like a certificate of trust: anyone he spoke to in the market was trusted with loans without witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: The master (leading sage) of the Land of Israel

steps.confusionAlert: The text prints רבי (אליעזר) in parentheses, but the correct reading is רבי אלעזר, the student of רבי יוחנן. Don't confuse him with the תנא רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: And would Reish Lakish speak
with Rabba bar bar Chana?
Just as Rabbi Elazar,
phrases.notes: Opens the 'if even this one, then certainly that one' argument; the correct reading is רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: who was the master of the Land of Israel,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא הֲוָה מִשְׁתַּעֵי רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ בַּהֲדֵיהּ,
phrases.english: and Reish Lakish would not speak with him,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמַאן דְּמִשְׁתַּעֵי רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ בַּהֲדֵיהּ בְּשׁוּקָא,
phrases.english: for anyone Reish Lakish spoke with in the marketplace,
people would give him a business loan without witnesses —
phrases.notes: Being seen with ריש לקיש proved a person was fully trustworthy.

phrases.aramaic: בַּהֲדֵי רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה מִשְׁתַּעֵי?!
phrases.english: would he speak with Rabba bar bar Chana?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, מִי מִשְׁתַּעֵי בַּהֲדֵי רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about the worm and the בת קול and returns to the original river story, challenging who was in it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The story's claim that ריש לקיש spoke with רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from רבי אלעזר: if ריש לקיש would not speak publicly with the greatest sage of ארץ ישראל, he surely would not speak with רבה בר בר חנה.

steps.title: רב פפא: Swap one of the people in the story
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that one of the two names must be replaced. Either it was ריש לקיש with זעירי, or it was רבה בר בר חנה with רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Put a different man between them. Either it was ריש לקיש together with זעירי, or it was רבה בר בר חנה together with רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא fixes the story by saying one of the names was mixed up. The pair was not ריש לקיש and רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two options. In the first, ריש לקיש was in the river and the great Babylonian sage זעירי gave him a hand, and ריש לקיש would speak with someone of זעירי's stature. In the second, רבה בר בר חנה was in the river and רבי אלעזר made the statement. Either way the content of the story stays the same; only the cast changes.

keyTerms.meaning: Throw a (different) man between them, i.e., replace one of the people

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, שְׁדִי גַּבְרָא בֵּינַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Cast a man between them:
Either it was Reish Lakish and Ze'iri,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה הֲוָה וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר.
phrases.english: or it was Rabba bar bar Chana and Rabbi Elazar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, שְׁדִי גַּבְרָא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 34 by changing the identity of one participant.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual correction: the names in the story are adjusted.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story involved ריש לקיש speaking with רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The story involved a different pair: ריש לקיש with זעירי, or רבה בר בר חנה with רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: That is not the real reason
steps.stepSummary: The statement was reported to רבי יוחנן. He rejected ריש לקיש's reason, saying that even if all the Jews had gone up with עזרא, the שכינה still would not have rested in the מקדש שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the man came before רבי יוחנן, רבי יוחנן said to him: That is not the reason. Even if all of them had gone up in the days of עזרא, the שכינה still would not have rested in the מקדש שני.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: the person who heard ריש לקיש's statement reported it to רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן disagreed with the reason ריש לקיש gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש had blamed the Babylonian Jews: because they did not all go up with עזרא, the שכינה did not rest in the מקדש שני. רבי יוחנן says their failure to go up was not the cause. The שכינה would not have rested there in any case, so the Babylonians are not to blame.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them went up (to ארץ ישראל)
In the days of עזרא (the return to build the מקדש שני)

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the meaning of the whole story. The missing שכינה is no longer a punishment for the Babylonian Jews. It becomes a built-in feature of the מקדש שני.

phrases.english: When he came before Rabbi Yochanan,
he said to him: That is not the reason,

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי סְלִיקוּ כּוּלְּהוּ בִּימֵי עֶזְרָא
phrases.english: even if they had all gone up in the days of Ezra

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲוָה שָׁרְיָא שְׁכִינָה בְּמִקְדָּשׁ שֵׁנִי,
phrases.english: the Divine Presence would not have rested in the Second Temple,

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָאו הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the cast of the story is settled, the story continues with רבי יוחנן's reaction to the statement made in the river.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reason (Babylonians not going up), not the fact that the שכינה was missing from the מקדש שני.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The Babylonians' failure to go up did not cause the lack of שכינה; it would have been missing even if they had all gone up.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's source: God beautifies יפת but dwells in the tents of שם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a פסוק as his source: 'God will enlarge יפת, and dwell in the tents of שם.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'God will enlarge (beautify) יפת, and He will dwell in the tents of שם.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן quotes a verse to back up his claim. The גמרא explains how the verse proves his point on the next amud, so this step sets up that explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse separates two things. יפת is given beauty, and the שכינה dwells only in the tents of שם. The coming explanation will connect יפת to Persia, whose king כורש enabled the building of the מקדש שני, while the שכינה rested only in a Temple built by the descendants of שם (the מקדש ראשון built by שלמה).

keyTerms.meaning: יפת, son of נח (ancestor of Persia)
The tents of שם (ancestor of Israel)

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש blamed the Babylonian Jews for the missing שכינה in the מקדש שני. רבי יוחנן says it was never going to rest there, and he points to the verse 'God will beautify יפת, and dwell in the tents of שם.'

phrases.english: as it is written: "God will enlarge Japheth,
and dwell in the tents of Shem" (Genesis 9:27),
phrases.notes: The explanation of how this proves the point continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״יַפְתְּ אֱלֹהִים לְיֶפֶת וְיִשְׁכֹּן בְּאׇהֳלֵי שֵׁם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural source for רבי יוחנן's claim in step 36.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that the שכינה would not rest in the מקדש שני regardless of how many people went up.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית ט:כז: 'יַפְתְּ אֱלֹהִים לְיֶפֶת וְיִשְׁכֹּן בְּאׇהֳלֵי שֵׁם'
